security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when the LSU issues HLV/HSV load/store requests, the TLB response carries the VS-stage leaf PTE permission bits (including X bit) in TlbPermBundle/TlbSectorPermBundle. If the unchecked-access decision for HLV/HSV is wired directly to `perm.x` from the TLB response (per the spec: 'HLV*/HSV* generate unchecked memory accesses if VS-stage leaf PTE entry's execute permission bit is set'), a malicious guest OS can set the X bit on data-page PTEs to force the hypervisor's HLV/HSV emulation to silently skip all MTE tag checks. The PTE.X bit is an architectural field already present in PtePermBundle (MMUBundle.scala:43) and propagated through TlbPermBundle.x (MMUBundle.scala:78) to the LSU, making it trivially guest-controllable through page table manipulation—no CSR corruption or privilege escalation needed. Additionally, the hstatus.MTAG_I bit (specified at a former WPRI slot in hstatus) does not exist in XiangShan's current HstatusBundle (HypervisorLevel.scala:231-245), so the entire HLV/HSV unchecked-access-on-MTAG_I path is unimplementable without CSR bit-layout redesign, leaving the PTE.X bypass as the only operable mechanism once minimally wired.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: TlbPermBundle.x wired to unchecked_loadstore signal in HLV/HSV datapath; missing privilege-level gate on PTE.X-based tag-check bypass; hstatus.MTAG_I field not allocated in HstatusBundle CSR layout; LSU perm.x passthrough to tag_check_enable without virtualization-mode qualification
security_spec.summary: HLV/HSV tag-check bypass gated on guest-controlled PTE.X creates architectural privilege-escalation backdoor: malicious guest marks data page executable to force hypervisor memory accesses to skip MTE tag validation, enabling undetectable guest-to-hypervisor memory poisoning through legitimate HLV/HSV emulation paths
